assumptions: The measurement certifies that SOME image in the binary serves an sm_89 device at full speed. It does not identify WHICH image the driver selected: by CUDA's documented minor-version rule the sm_86 cubin (major 8, minor 6 <= 9) is loadable on sm_89 and is the expected choice, and the absence of any JIT stall at load supports it, but this job did not measure the selection directly (a CUDA_FORCE_PTX_JIT=1 control run would).
The net under test is randomly initialised, so the figure certifies the engine and the device, not playing strength.

2401.88 vs 2322.17 visits/s is a single-thread, batch-size-1, 819k-parameter workload: it is latency-bound, so it does NOT mean an L40S out-throughputs a B200 in the production self-play regime (many threads, batched evaluation). It bounds the JIT/fallback question only.
The b7c96h3tfrs export used here is the exact artifact of job 298018; a re-export would change the sha256 without invalidating the claim.
cuDNN comes from the nvidia-cudnn-cu12 pip wheel inside R/venv; anything running the binary must keep that lib dir on LD_LIBRARY_PATH, which R/env.sh does.

candidate_obligation_row.text: Every partition in mission.json compute.partitions must have a GPU architecture the engine binary can execute. The check is NOT 'an exact sm_XY image is present' -- job 300987 measured an L40S (sm_89) running the mission binary at 2401.88 visits/s from an arch list that contains no sm_89, because CUDA loads a cubin built for X.y on a device X.z with z >= y. The check IS: for each allowed partition, the device's compute-capability MAJOR must appear in `cuobjdump --list-elf $KATAGO_BIN` with a MINOR no greater than the device's, or the binary must be rebuilt with that architecture added to cpp/CMakeLists.txt (codes/env/cmake-sm100.diff is the precedent for sm_100; codes/env/cmake-sm89.diff is authored and dry-run verified for sm_89 but was not needed). Re-run codes/env/l40s_probe.sbatch, re-pointed at the new partition, whenever a partition is added to mission.json compute.partitions.
